title: Turf species, mowing height and lawn health
audience: Lawn and turf crews and supervisors who mow, edge and assess lawns for clients across residential, strata and commercial sites.
learningOutcomes: Identify the common turf types on a site and state how their growth habit affects mowing.
Set a mowing height appropriate to the species, season and site conditions.
Recognise early signs of poor lawn health, including compaction, thatch build-up, water stress, pests and disease.
Describe safe mower operation on slopes, around obstacles and near people and pets.

instruction.heading: Turf is a living surface
instruction.body: A lawn is a planted surface that responds to every cut, every walk across it and every change in water and nutrition. The crew who mows it is the most frequent visitor, so the crew's habits shape the result. A lawn that is cut too short or with blunt blades becomes stressed, thins out and invites weeds. A lawn that is never cut becomes uneven and the client expects a rescue. Good lawn work starts with knowing what the turf is, what height it should be kept at and what it looks like when it is healthy. Identify the species before you mow, because two lawns of similar appearance may need very different heights and care.

instruction.heading: Identifying the common turf types
instruction.body: Lawns across Australia commonly contain warm-season grasses such as couch, kikuyu, buffalo and zoysia, and cool-season grasses such as perennial ryegrass and tall fescue. Warm-season grasses are usually active in warmer months and may go dormant in cold periods. Cool-season grasses are usually most active in cooler months. Many lawns are mixed, and weeds can be mistaken for turf. Look at the leaf width, colour, runner pattern, stolon and rhizome habit, and the seedhead if present. Check the client's notes for the species they have been told they have. If you cannot confirm the species, record the uncertainty and mow at a height that does not stress the turf. The species list in this draft is a working guide and is not verified against a named reference. Confirm it with a local turf guide or a qualified turf advisor before relying on it for a height recommendation.

instruction.heading: Setting the mowing height
instruction.body: The mowing height is the most important single setting on a lawn mower. Cutting too low removes too much leaf, weakens the roots and exposes the soil to heat. Adjust the height gradually when a lawn has been neglected, and do not drop it by a large amount in one pass. Set the height on a level surface and check it on each wheel. Note that high-traffic lawns and shaded lawns usually need a different height from open sunny lawns.

instruction.heading: Lawn health checks
instruction.body: Walk the lawn before mowing and look for signs of stress. Compaction shows as soil that is hard to push a screwdriver into, water that pools after rain and thin grass in paths. Thatch is a layer of dead and living stems and roots between the soil and the leaf, and it shows as a spongy surface and brown patches. Water stress shows as blue-grey leaves that do not spring back and dry patches that remain after watering. Pests such as lawn grubs and caterpillars cause patchy dieback that can be pulled up like a loose carpet. Disease shows as rings, spots or discoloured patches that are not explained by dogs, traffic or fuel spills. Record what you see, and do not diagnose a pest or disease without a clear identification. Refer the question to the client and to a qualified advisor, and do not apply a product under this lesson.

instruction.heading: Mower safety on the lawn
instruction.body: Mowers can throw objects, cut feet and fingers, tip on slopes and cause injury when refuelled or restarted with the blade still turning. Walk the lawn before you mow and remove sticks, stones, pet waste, toys, hoses and cords. Keep children and pets indoors or well away from the mowing zone. On slopes, follow the manufacturer's guidance and the business's slope rule, and mow across the face rather than up and down where the machine is unstable. Do not mow on wet or very steep ground where the mower can slip. Clean the blade and the deck when you have finished. Refuel only when the engine is off and cool, and keep fuel away from the mower's hot parts. Switch off and disconnect or remove the battery before clearing a blockage or checking the blade. Use eye and hearing protection and footwear with grip.

instruction.heading: Verification and escalation
instruction.body: A supervisor should check the height, the finish and the safety set-up. A competent worker can name the species they have identified, explain how they set the height, point to the signs of stress they checked for and describe the safe operation of the mower on a slope. Escalate any lawn that shows widespread dieback, any suspected pest or disease, any lawn where the species is uncertain and the height cannot be confirmed, and any slope that the mower cannot safely work.

procedure: Confirm the lawn's species from the client's notes and a visual check, and record any uncertainty.
Walk the lawn and remove debris, pet waste, toys, cords and hoses from the mowing zone.
Check for compaction, thatch, water stress, pests and disease, and record what you observe.
Set the mowing height from the approved reference or the client's written preference, and check each wheel on level ground.
Mow across slopes rather than up and down, and avoid wet or very steep ground.
Keep people and pets well away from the mowing zone, and stop if anyone enters it.
Switch off and disconnect or remove the battery before clearing a blockage or checking the blade.
Clean the deck and blade, and record the mowing height, the condition of the lawn and any referral.

workedExamples.situation: A client's lawn has been cut very short for several weeks by a previous contractor. It now looks yellow in patches and some areas are bare.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What height do you set, and what do you tell the client?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not drop the lawn to the target height in one pass. Raise the mower to a higher setting and reduce it gradually over several cuts, as the species and season allow. Record the stress signs, check for compaction and thatch, and tell the client that bare patches may need a separate plan. Do not apply a product or make a repair promise under this lesson. Refer the bare areas to the supervisor for a separate scope.

workedExamples.situation: A lawn on a steep bank has several sprinkler heads and a child's ball in the grass. A neighbour's dog is in the next yard, close to the fence.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do before mowing?
workedExamples.reasoning: Remove the ball and mark the sprinkler heads so the blade does not hit them. Ask the owner to keep the dog inside, and keep the mowing zone clear of people. Mow across the slope if the mower is stable on it, and stop if the machine feels unsafe. Do not mow up and down the bank. Record the hazards and the decisions made.

equipmentAndPpe: Mower with a sharp blade, inspected before use
Rake and hand tools for debris clearance
Turf identification guide or reference, approved by the business
Job sheet for recording height and lawn condition

commonErrors.error: Cutting the lawn to a very short height in one pass to make it look neat.
commonErrors.prevention: Remove only part of the leaf per cut and lower the height gradually across several mows.

commonErrors.error: Mowing with a blunt blade, which tears the leaf and leaves a brown edge.
commonErrors.prevention: Sharpen or replace the blade on the business schedule, and check the blade before each job.

commonErrors.error: Mowing up and down a slope where the machine can tip.
commonErrors.prevention: Follow the slope rule, mow across the face where the machine is stable, and stop when unsafe.

commonErrors.error: Diagnosing a pest or disease from a single patch and applying a product.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the observation, refer the diagnosis to a qualified advisor and do not apply products under this lesson.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Mower operation falls under the model WHS framework's duty to manage plant risk, to the level that is reasonably practicable. Guarding, slope controls and safe refuelling are part of that duty.
This lesson does not authorise the application of pesticides, herbicides or fertilisers. Product use is covered by the licence and authority rules in the lawn product lesson.

qualityStandard: The species is recorded or the uncertainty is noted, and the mowing height has been set from an approved reference or a written client preference.
No more than the agreed fraction of leaf has been removed in any single cut.
The mowing zone was cleared of hazards and people before mowing began.
Lawn condition and any referral are recorded at the end of the job.
documentationEvidence: Job record with the species, the mowing height, the date and the blade check.
Lawn condition record showing the signs of stress observed, with photographs taken with consent.
Referral record for any suspected pest, disease or widespread dieback.
Equipment inspection record for the mower and the blade.
summary: Identify the species, because the height and the care depend on it.
Remove only part of the leaf per cut, and lower heights gradually.
Look for compaction, thatch, water stress, pests and disease, and refer what you cannot confirm.
Mow across slopes where stable, keep people and pets clear, and switch off before clearing blockages.

knowledgeChecks.question: A lawn has been cut very short for weeks and now shows patchy yellowing. What is the best first step when setting the mowing height?
options: Set the mower to the lowest setting so the lawn looks even and tidy for the client on the day
Raise the height and lower it gradually over several mows, recording the stress signs.
Scalp the lawn once to remove the yellow tips and then leave it to recover on its own now

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is a sharp mower blade important?
options: A sharp blade cuts faster, so the lawn needs fewer passes and the job is done sooner today
A blunt blade is safer because it throws less debris and the crew needs less protective gear
A sharp blade cuts the leaf cleanly and avoids tearing that causes brown edges and stress.

knowledgeChecks.question: The mower is on a steep bank. What is the correct way to mow it?
options: Mow across the face where the machine is stable, and stop if the machine feels unsafe.
Mow straight up and down the bank for the cleanest line and the most even cut on the slope
Mow while walking backwards so the machine is pulled rather than pushed.
